big-news.text: The budget talks are still stuck. Ap, SV, Rødt, MDG and Sp were far apart on Saturday, and the hardest fight is Sp's demand for lower fuel taxes versus the climate cuts MDG and SV want. The budget has to reach Stortinget by Nov 30. Rødt looks set to win on dental care, with the next expansion starting with older people.

whats-changing.text: The budget proposal raises the air passenger tax on flights within Europe to 126 kr per trip, up from 61 kr. SAS also drops its direct Trondheim–Bodø–Tromsø routes from mid-December.
A beer in the park is still illegal. The health authorities advise against allowing it, and the government hasn't said when it will put forward a proposal. Høyre wants it in place by next summer.

oslo.text: Today is the last day of the T-bane shutdown. Normal service is back from the first departure on Monday.
Several cars burned overnight at Galgeberg and Rodeløkka, and police have arrested and charged a man in his 40s.
Oslo's Christmas tree for London, a 21 m spruce from Sørkedalen nicknamed "Jolly Cheery," has been cut down. It will be lit on Trafalgar Square on Dec 3.

be-aware.text: Statens vegvesen warns that roads can look bare but still have a thin layer of ice, especially in the morning, evening and night. Take care on the roads.
Vy trains on Østlandet have been crowded and cancelled after brake problems, with no fix date as of Thursday. Travel outside rush hour if you can.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: Jul i Vinterland at Spikersuppa is free to enter and open today 10:00–20:00. The all-rides ticket is 199 kr, so the rides aren't free.
The Christmas market at Vestre Aker menighetshus (Ullevålsveien 117B) is free, today 12:00–15:30, with crafts, baking, a café and a raffle.
Next Sunday, Nov 29, the Christmas tree on Universitetsplassen is lit from 17:00 to 19:00, with a choir. It's free.
